failure_summary.description: Skill has no guidance on the repo's executable function-contract pattern (`export const X = Fn(...)` with `X.implementSync(...)`), so the agent invented an ad-hoc S.Class-based 'schema transform' instead of the required Fn contract, failing two required-pattern completion checks.
Skill's 'Verify before finishing' step never mentions running the repo formatter/linter (biome), so the agent only ran a standalone tsc check and shipped a file that failed the biome format check.

patch.reasoning: The single failed trajectory lost most of its score to two distinct, generalizable gaps rather than fixture-specific details. First, the task asked for an 'executable function contract' alongside a schema-owned input model, and the scorer required the canonical repo pattern `export const <Name> = Fn(...)` plus `<Name>.implementSync(...)` — but the skill's schema guidance stops at data modeling (S.Class/S.Struct, tagged unions, Option handling) and never teaches that executable/function-shaped exports use the Fn contract-and-implement pattern instead of a bespoke schema transform. Adding this as a Fast Rule closes a real rule_missing gap that generalizes to any task asking for a schema-owned 'function contract' or 'executable contract', not just this fixture's naming. Second, the agent treated a standalone tsc invocation as sufficient verification and skipped the repo formatter, so the biome check failed independently of the schema/type work. The skill's 'Verify before finishing' checklist is entirely about schema shape and never mentions formatting/lint parity with the repo's own tooling, which is a rule_missing gap of similar generality (any fixture-edit task will hit this). One combined edit addresses both without hardcoding this task's names.

edits.target: - Prefer built-in schema constructors and checks before `S.makeFilter(...)`.
edits.content:
- When a task asks for an executable function contract alongside a schema-owned
  input model (e.g. "executable function contract", "function contract",
  "implement/execute this against the schema"), export it as
  `export const <Name> = Fn(...)` and implement it with
  `<Name>.implementSync(...)` (or the async/effectful `implement` variant for
  effectful bodies) instead of writing an ad-hoc schema transform or plain
  function — check `references/pattern-catalog.md` or local repo examples for
  the exact `Fn(...)` signature before writing one from memory.
- Before finishing, run the repo's formatter/linter (e.g. `biome check`) on
  every edited file, not just a standalone type-check — a passing `tsc`/`tsgo`
  run does not imply the file matches repo formatting, and formatting
  violations are scored independently of type and schema-law checks.
